findings.title: Runtime databases and caches were tracked by Git
findings.evidence: Git tracked local SQLite snapshots, long-term-memory data, fridge inventory, and runtime cache files.
findings.recommendation: Keep runtime data local and ignored; retain only the static shelf-life defaults resource.
acceptanceCriteria: Runtime files remain on local disk
git ls-files no longer returns the runtime files
git check-ignore identifies an explicit rule for each file

findings.title: Development dependency audit failed on newly disclosed vulnerabilities
findings.evidence: The baseline full npm audit reported four high and one moderate development dependency vulnerabilities; the production-only audit was clean.
findings.recommendation: Apply non-forced patch updates and keep protobufjs on the patched 7.6.x line.
acceptanceCriteria: npm audit --audit-level=high exits zero
npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high reports zero vulnerabilities
No forced major upgrade is introduced

findings.title: Formatting gate was blocked by generated architecture output and source drift
findings.evidence: The baseline formatting check failed for 49 files, including multi-megabyte Golden Goose generated artifacts and hand-maintained source files.
findings.recommendation: Exclude immutable generated snapshots and format all hand-maintained source, tests, configuration, and documentation.
acceptanceCriteria: npm run format:check exits zero
git diff --check exits zero

findings.title: Human architecture documentation described obsolete persistence paths
findings.evidence: The prior documents still presented Firebase/localStorage as the primary production flow even though startup configures authenticated FastAPI API adapters.
findings.recommendation: Use current source, OpenAPI, migrations, and the dual-runtime contract as the documentation source of truth.
acceptanceCriteria: Server MySQL/manual-account behavior is documented
Desktop SQLite/no-login behavior is documented
Legacy adapters are identified as non-production

findings.title: Audit findings catalog contained a non-existent demo source
findings.evidence: The baseline findings catalog referenced the non-existent example path src/web/cart.tsx instead of repository evidence.
findings.recommendation: Replace example findings with evidence-backed audit records and keep Markdown and JSON identifiers aligned.
acceptanceCriteria: Every finding references repository evidence
Markdown and JSON finding identifiers match

findings.title: Generated architecture snapshot is partial and not current
findings.evidence: The Golden Goose snapshot records source commit 0122bc and completeness=partial; generated JSON files add roughly 34 MB to the checkout.
findings.recommendation: Treat the snapshot as historical until regenerated at the current commit; evaluate external artifact storage separately.
acceptanceCriteria: Human documentation labels the snapshot historical and partial
No current architecture claim relies solely on the generated snapshot

findings.title: Real MySQL and server E2E validation passed in disposable local Docker
findings.evidence: Docker Desktop 29.5.3 ran MySQL 8.0.46 (mysql:8.0) in the repository disposable compose stack; a fresh database migrated to 20260719_0008, one MySQL contract test passed, and two server authentication/isolation E2E tests passed in the final 31.297-second run.
findings.recommendation: Keep npm run test:server:local as the repeatable local acceptance gate and retain CI MySQL validation; never point these commands at production or real user data.
acceptanceCriteria: Fresh MySQL migrates to Alembic head
MySQL contract test passes
Server authentication/isolation E2E passes

findings.title: Runtime schema creation could mask an incomplete database at the recorded migration head
findings.evidence: Service constructors could call create_all after the Alembic revision check, allowing a partial schema with a forged head to start and mutate in place.
findings.recommendation: Keep runtime schema creation disabled and require both Alembic head and a read-only schema fingerprint before serving requests.
acceptanceCriteria: A partial database at the expected head fails closed
The failed startup does not change database bytes or tables

findings.title: Server Fridge cache and provider accounting could cross tenant boundaries
findings.evidence: Provider notes were stored in a shared runtime cache and receipt provider calls bypassed per-user AI rate, budget, and usage accounting.
findings.recommendation: Keep server runtime cache disabled and route every real receipt provider call through a request-scoped metered client.
acceptanceCriteria: One user cannot receive another user's cached provider notes
Blocked receipt calls do not invoke the provider and attempted provider calls are metered

findings.title: E2E tooling could target an ordinary database and hide cleanup failure
findings.evidence: Server E2E accepted an ordinary application database fallback and the MySQL aggregate script could warn yet exit successfully when final Docker cleanup failed.
findings.recommendation: Require an explicit dedicated test URL at launcher and seed boundaries, isolate desktop environment variables, and propagate cleanup failure.
acceptanceCriteria: Only an explicit MySQL test/e2e database is accepted
Desktop E2E strips inherited database and seed variables
Cleanup failure makes the aggregate gate fail

findings.title: Calendar imports and references could leave partial or orphaned state
findings.evidence: Local snapshot import committed entities independently and CRUD accepted missing or cross-tenant calendar relationships.
findings.recommendation: Keep strict nested DTO prevalidation, same-tenant reference checks, one import transaction, delete cleanup, backup validation, and integrity repair as defense in depth.
acceptanceCriteria: Late import failure rolls back every entity
Missing and cross-tenant references return 422 without writes
Integrity repair nulls nullable orphan links without deleting business records

findings.title: Tool activation created goal and project in two non-atomic writes
findings.evidence: A successful goal request followed by a failed project request left a durable orphan and retry could duplicate the goal.
findings.recommendation: Keep goal and project creation in one backend transaction and add durable idempotency before supporting automatic retries.
acceptanceCriteria: Project insertion failure leaves no goal
Every production activation path calls the compound endpoint

findings.title: Obsolete asynchronous reads and AI results could overwrite current state
findings.evidence: Out-of-order calendar ranges, memory overview/details, cross-conversation AI responses, and reads completing after successful writes could replace newer user state.
findings.recommendation: Invalidate request generations on new loads, resets, account changes, selection changes, new conversations, and successful writes.
acceptanceCriteria: Older deferred results never replace the latest selection or write
Obsolete failures do not set current error/loading state

findings.title: Recurrence and local AI date conversion drifted across timezone and DST boundaries
findings.evidence: Recurrence occurrence/until dates used UTC slices, future AI dates reused the current offset, and a nonexistent spring-forward local time silently shifted by one hour.
findings.recommendation: Use local calendar dates, resolve target wall-clock time with an IANA timezone, and reject nonexistent local times explicitly.
acceptanceCriteria: Recurrence this/following targets the local occurrence date
Future dates use the target date offset
Spring-forward nonexistent times are rejected

findings.title: Calendar hour intent and modal keyboard focus were incomplete
findings.evidence: The TimeGrid add control ignored the clicked hour and remained visually hidden on keyboard focus; the shared modal lacked initial focus, a trap, and focus restoration.
findings.recommendation: Preserve the clicked time range through the creation intent and keep the shared modal keyboard contract covered by component tests.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking or focusing a 3 PM slot prefills 15:00
Modal focus is trapped and restored after Escape

findings.title: Public write endpoints accepted loose types and could surface database errors as 500
findings.evidence: Preferences, Fridge, Memory, Goal Control, AI context, calendar, and tool preset payloads included raw dictionary or coercive numeric/text paths; tool preset PATCH also replaced complete records with partial JSON.
findings.recommendation: Keep strict DTO or explicit allowlist validation aligned with database limits and merge partial preset updates into the stored complete record.
acceptanceCriteria: Wrong types, unknown fields, invalid dates, non-finite values, and empty patches return 422
Rejected payloads do not write
Tool preset PATCH preserves required fields

findings.title: Tauri discarded structured backend recovery handshakes
findings.evidence: The sidecar emitted CALENDAR_BACKEND_RECOVERY JSON but the Tauri startup parser only recognized READY and reduced recovery to a generic exit message.
findings.recommendation: Preserve typed recovery code, message, database, backup, diagnostic paths, and extra payload through the desktop startup error.
acceptanceCriteria: READY and RECOVERY are parsed independently
Malformed handshakes fail explicitly
Recovery paths remain available to the UI/error surface

findings.title: Python and test catalog gates could validate a different environment or stale source
findings.evidence: Backend, OpenAPI, audit, MySQL, and E2E commands could use PATH Python; the catalog referenced a missing schema and stale or incorrect trigger paths without an exact current-content provenance gate.
findings.recommendation: Use the fail-closed repository test interpreter, validate catalog schema and Goose mappings, and bind clean checkouts to the exact Git-filtered worktree hash.
acceptanceCriteria: No Python validation command silently falls back to PATH
Every catalog suite maps to one Goose command
Exact worktree hash drift fails

findings.title: Unbounded Vitest workers made the full suite flaky under contention
findings.evidence: A Goal Planner integration case timed out only in the full suite while passing in isolation, consistent with worker/resource contention.
findings.recommendation: Keep a bounded worker count and optimize individual slow cases before raising timeouts broadly.
acceptanceCriteria: The complete Vitest suite passes with the bounded worker setting
Focused Goal Planner behavior remains covered
